blocks.title: Present perfect simple vs continuous · B2

items.en: I have written three emails this morning — here they are.
items.cz: Dnes ráno jsem napsal tři emaily — tady jsou.
items.gap: I ____ three emails this morning — here they are. (write)
accepts: I have written three emails this morning — here they are.
I've written three emails this morning — here they are.
I have written three emails this morning — here they're.
I've written three emails this morning — here they're.
items.explanation: Three emails, and here they are: a finished count with a result → have written.
items.explanation_cz: Tři hotové emaily a výsledek → have written.

items.en: I have been writing emails all morning and I still have two left.
items.cz: Už celé dopoledne píšu emaily a pořád mi zbývají dva.
items.gap: I ____ emails all morning and I still have two left. (write)
accepts: I have been writing emails all morning and I still have two left.
I've been writing emails all morning and I still have two left.
items.explanation: Two still left, so the writing is unfinished — the time it has taken is the point → have been writing.
items.explanation_cz: Zbývají dva, psaní není hotové — jde o dobu → have been writing.

items.en: She has read the whole report — she can answer now.
items.cz: Už přečetla celou zprávu — teď může odpovídat.

items.explanation: The whole report is read and she can answer → the result counts: has read.
items.explanation_cz: Celá zpráva je přečtená a může odpovídat → počítá se výsledek: has read.

items.en: She has been reading the report for an hour and she is only on page two.
items.cz: Tu zprávu čte už hodinu a je teprve na straně dvě.

items.explanation: Only on page two: after an hour the reading is still running → has been reading.
items.explanation_cz: Teprve na straně dvě: po hodině čtení stále běží → has been reading.

items.en: They have painted the kitchen — it looks new.
items.cz: Kuchyň už vymalovali — vypadá nově.

accepts: They have painted the kitchen — it looks new.

items.explanation: The kitchen looks new — the painting is done and you can see it → have painted.
items.explanation_cz: Kuchyň vypadá nově — malování je hotové a je to vidět → have painted.

items.en: They have been painting the kitchen all day and it is still not finished.
items.cz: Už celý den malují kuchyň a pořád to není hotové.

items.explanation: Still not finished after a whole day → the process, not the result: have been painting.

items.en: How many times have you visited Prague?
items.cz: Kolikrát jsi byl v Praze?

accepts: How many times have you visited Prague?
items.explanation: How many times counts finished visits → present perfect simple: have you visited.
items.explanation_cz: How many times počítá hotové návštěvy → have you visited.

items.en: How long have you been waiting here?
items.cz: Jak dlouho tady čekáš?
items.gap: How long ____ here? (wait)
accepts: How long have you been waiting here?
items.explanation: How long asks for duration up to now → present perfect continuous: have you been waiting.
items.explanation_cz: How long se ptá na dobu až do teď → have you been waiting.

items.explanation_cz: Po celém odpoledni všude prach → úklid není hotový: have been cleaning.

  <line x1="30" y1="200" x2="510" y2="200" stroke="var(--muted, #a0a0a0)" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <circle cx="120" cy="56" r="7" fill="var(--text, #eaeaea)"/>

  <path d="M 127 118 L 396 118" stroke="var(--text, #eaeaea)" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>

  <rect x="113" y="163" width="287" height="20" rx="10" fill="var(--vocab-accent, #4db6c7)"/>

  <text x="30" y="196" font-size="11" fill="var(--muted, #a0a0a0)">present perfect continuous · still running at now</text>

points: Both reach up to **now** — that is what makes them perfect tenses.
Simple marks a **result** or a **count**: I have written three emails.
Continuous marks the **time spent**: I have been writing all morning.
Past simple stays back there with no link to now.

rows: a finished point, no link to now

cards.title: The two shapes

table.caption: Present perfect simple vs continuous
rows: how many · already · done · result now
how long · for · since · all… · still going

points: Simple: **have written** · has finished · haven't done
Continuous: **have been** writing · has been waiting · haven't been sleeping
The participle and the -ing come from the same verb — only the shape changes.

cards.title: Simple = result / count / done

rows: a result you can see now
She **has read** the whole report — she can answer now.
She **has made** ten cakes this week for the sale.
How many emails **have** you sent today?

points: The activity is over. What is left is the **outcome**.
Words that go with it: **already** · **just** · **yet** · how many · three times.

cards.title: Continuous = process / duration

rows: They **have been** painting the kitchen all day and it is still not finished.
She **has been** teaching since eight o'clock and she has not had a break.
He **has been** running for forty minutes and he looks tired.

points: The activity itself is the point — **how long**, not how many.
Words that go with it: **for** · **since** · all day · all morning · still.

cards.title: How many vs How long

rows: How many times **have** you visited Prague?
How long **have** you been waiting here?

points: The question word usually picks the aspect before you read the rest.

cards.title: Four shapes, one fits

rows: — and I still have two left.

points: The four shapes look alike. The words around the gap choose between them.
Read to the end of the line before you answer.

cards.title: Common mistakes

rows: I **have been** writing emails all morning.
How long **have** you been waiting here?
~~She has been reading the whole report, she can answer.~~
She **has read** the whole report — she can answer now.

points: Czech uses one present tense for both ideas, so the -ing form feels safe. It is not.
